sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. Rate limiting never runs: no Redis call, and no counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: The budget is per customer ID, not per key, so the three keys share one budget: 100 requests per minute if Standard. Enterprise has no limit set yet, so it is not rate limited.
sonnet.q3: It gets 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The backend never sees the request; it is never forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. Rejected requests cost nothing, and the counter is not incremented.
sonnet.q5: Yes. Passed requests always count, even if the backend fails. Nothing is refunded.
sonnet.q6: It fails open. The gateway forwards the request, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and adds no rate-limit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. Enterprise is undecided (a config value with no default). While it is unset, Enterprise requests skip the check.
sonnet.q8: The counts live in one shared Redis, under the key rl:{customerId}:{floor(redisNow/60)}. The key expires after 120 s, and that removes old counts.
sonnet.q9: The window is a fixed calendar minute from the Redis clock. A new minute uses a new key, so the count starts again at 0 when the minute rolls over.
sonnet.q10: The check is one atomic Lua script. Redis runs scripts one at a time, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Retry-After is 60 - (redisNow mod 60) whole seconds, from 1 to 60. It is sent only on 429.
sonnet.q12: The document does not say the gateway retries the store, and the Redis call has a 50 ms timeout. The client gets the backend's response with no X-RateLimit headers, so it gets no rate-limit information.
